primary_diagnosis: NSAID‑induced acute‑on‑chronic kidney injury (AKI on CKD‑4)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient is a 72‑year‑old female with stage‑4 diabetic CKD, resistant hypertension, CAD, and extensive polypharmacy. The most urgent active driver is NSAID‑induced acute‑on‑chronic kidney injury, given ongoing naproxen use in the setting of severe baseline renal impairment. Resistant hypertension with volume overload follows closely, as uncontrolled BP accelerates both renal and cardiac decline. The underlying chronic disease (diabetic nephropathy) remains a major substrate, while electrolyte disturbances, CAD, HFpEF, and other comorbidities contribute to overall risk. Missing current labs (electrolytes, BNP, BP trends), medication details, and cardiac imaging limit precise quantification of several diagnoses, prompting targeted work‑up.

recommended_workup: Repeat comprehensive renal panel: serum creatinine, eGFR, BUN, electrolytes (K⁺, Na⁺, HCO₃⁻), calcium, phosphate, PTH, and urine protein‑to‑creatinine ratio
Complete blood count with iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation, reticulocyte count)
Basic metabolic panel to assess for hyper‑/hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis
Blood pressure home monitoring log and physical exam for signs of volume overload (edema, JVP, lung crackles); obtain BNP
Full medication reconciliation including over‑the‑counter and herbal products; focus on anti‑seizure, antihyperglycemic, and potassium‑sparing agents
Repeat A1c and fasting glucose; review antidiabetic regimen; consider continuous glucose monitoring for hypoglycemia detection
Transthoracic echocardiogram with diastolic function assessment to evaluate for HFpEF and LV mass
Stress test or coronary CT angiography if CAD progression is suspected
Lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides) and initiate/adjust statin therapy as indicated
Screen for depression and anxiety (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) and refer to mental‑health services if positive
Obstructive sleep apnea screening (STOP‑BANG) and consider polysomnography
Vaccination review (hepatitis B, pneumococcal, influenza, COVID‑19) and serologic testing for hepatitis B/C, HIV, TB
Functional and frailty assessment (gait speed, grip strength, ADL questionnaire)
Urine toxicology and referral to addiction medicine for ongoing substance‑use disorder
